Validation — Compare Against Your Baseline

Compare today’s photo of your room with yesterday’s. Anything missing? Find it now, not next week.

admin@fw-01(active)> show system info | match "sw-version|app-version|threat-version"  PAN-OS version plus the two content versions
admin@fw-01(active)> show chassis-ready                                       is the DATAPLANE up — 'yes' means it can pass traffic, not just answer SSH
admin@fw-01(active)> show high-availability state                             the main HA summary — roles, sync status, link health
admin@fw-01(active)> show high-availability all                               full HA detail — use this when something looks wrong
admin@fw-01(active)> show session info                                        session count and how full the session table is
admin@fw-01(active)> show session all                                         list live sessions — proof the box is actually passing traffic
admin@fw-01(active)> show interface all                                       every interface and whether it is up — compare to your baseline
admin@fw-01(active)> show routing route                                       the routing table — confirm neighbours came back after reboot
admin@fw-01(active)> show vpn ike-sa                                          IPsec phase 1 — are tunnels negotiating
admin@fw-01(active)> show vpn ipsec-sa                                        IPsec phase 2 — are tunnels actually passing data
admin@fw-01(active)> show system resources                                    live CPU and memory, like top on Linux
admin@fw-01(active)> show counter global filter severity drop                 global drop counters — what the firewall is discarding and why
admin@fw-01(active)> show log system direction equal backward                 newest system log entries first
CheckPass condition
sw-versionMatches the target, on both peers.
chassis-readyyes.
HA stateOne active, one passive (or both active in A/A). Config synchronized.
Session countIn the same ballpark as your baseline, and climbing.
InterfacesSame set up as before. A missing link is a hardware or config problem, not a fluke.
Routing / VPNNeighbours re-established, tunnels re-keyed.
System logNo repeating errors, no process restarts.
PreemptionBack to whatever it was before you started.
  • Version: Dashboard → General Information. HA: Dashboard → High Availability widget.
  • Sessions: Monitor → Traffic (new entries arriving). Errors: Monitor → Logs → System.
  • Routing: Network → Virtual Routers → More Runtime Stats (Advanced Routing: Network → Routing → Logical Routers → More Runtime Stats).
  • VPN: Network → IPSec Tunnels — status lights green.
Upgrade · Validate, Roll Back, FixVALIDATION ✓ checked vs PAN docs Runbook

Validation, Part 2: Compare ARP and Routing with the Baseline

Walk the same street and wave at the same neighbours. Anyone who doesn't wave back gets a knock on the door.

Run exactly the same commands as in Baseline Capture, Part 2 on each peer, log them to <hostname>-POST-<date>.txt, then compare the two files.

Step 1 · Wake up the critical next hops first

After a reboot the ARP table starts empty and fills only as traffic flows. An idle host shows as missing until something talks to it. Ping each critical next hop from the dataplane before you compare:

admin@fw-01(active)> ping source 198.51.100.2 host 198.51.100.1  ISP gateway, sourced from the WAN interface IP
admin@fw-01(active)> ping source 10.10.20.1 host 10.10.20.254  core switch, sourced from the inside interface IP
admin@fw-01(active)> show arp all  now compare with the PRE file

Step 2 · Compare

ComparePassIf not
Critical next hops in show arp allEvery one is c (complete) again, with the same MACIncomplete: interface, VLAN tag or the neighbour itself (ARP & Neighbours group). Different MAC: a device was swapped or HA moved. Clear the neighbour's ARP cache if it still points at the old MAC.
Static ARP entriesAll presentRe-check the configuration was preserved.
Route count per VR/LRSame as the baseline, give or take dynamic churnFind which prefixes are missing (compare the two files), then check the protocol that should provide them.
Static and path-monitored routesSame routes active (flag A)Path monitor target unreachable, or interface down (Routing Core group).
BGP peersAll Established, prefix counts like beforeBGP group: state machine and playbook.
OSPF neighboursAll FullOSPF group: adjacency states (ExStart = MTU).
Per-VSYS session countsClimbing back towards the baselineCheck the VSYS's VR and interfaces first.

Quick comparison on your laptop

// Linux / macOS
diff fw-01-PRE-27Oct.txt fw-01-POST-27Oct.txt
// Windows PowerShell
Compare-Object (Get-Content fw-01-PRE-27Oct.txt) (Get-Content fw-01-POST-27Oct.txt)

Timers and ages always differ, so expect noise in a raw diff. What matters is entries that disappeared, changed from complete to incomplete, or changed MAC, and route or prefix counts that dropped.

Upgrade · Validate, Roll Back, FixSESSION SYNC ✓ checked vs PAN docs Runbook

Confirming Session Sync Actually Resumed

Are the friends still passing notes? Count the notes. If the count does not go up, they stopped talking.

HA can report healthy while session synchronisation is silently dead. The HA2 interface counters are the proof.

admin@fw-01(active)> show high-availability interface ha2          HA2 counters — proof session sync is actually running
check the CPU table hardware interface counters are incrementing

admin@fw-01(active)> show high-availability state-synchronization  session-sync statistics between the peers
ConfigurationExpected counter behaviour
Active/passive — active peerPackets transmitted increasing.
Active/passive — passive peerPackets received only.
Active/passive with HA2 keep-aliveBoth transmit and receive on the passive peer — keep-alive is bidirectional.
Active/active — both peersBoth transmit and receive.

If HA2 counters are flat, the next failover will drop every established session. This check costs thirty seconds and is skipped in most upgrade runbooks.

  • No GUI equivalent for HA2 hardware counters — this one is CLI only.
Upgrade · Validate, Roll Back, FixROLLBACK ✓ checked vs PAN docs Runbook

Reverting to a Previous Maintenance Release

Going back one small step on the same staircase is easy — the old shoes are still by the door.

Same feature release, earlier maintenance or hotfix — for example 11.1.4-h13 back to 11.1.4-h7. This is the easy case: the firewall keeps an automatic configuration snapshot from before the upgrade and restores it on the way down.

admin@fw-01(active)> request system software info                             list versions available to download, with a Downloaded flag
confirm the older version is still present on disk

admin@fw-01(active)> request system software install version <previous-version>  install the older image to roll back — still needs a reboot
admin@fw-01(active)> show jobs id <jobid>                                     poll one job — wait for Status FIN and Result OK
admin@fw-01(active)> request restart system                                   reboot NOW — no confirmation, no grace period

after reboot:
admin@fw-01(active)> show system info | match sw-version                      just the running PAN-OS version
admin@fw-01(active)> show chassis-ready                                       is the DATAPLANE up — 'yes' means it can pass traffic, not just answer SSH

In an HA pair, roll back the same way you upgraded: suspend, install, reboot, functional, one peer at a time. Do not roll back both simultaneously — that is a full outage and it gives you nothing.

  • Device → Software → Install on the previous version (still Downloaded) → Reboot. HA: one peer at a time, as for the upgrade.
Upgrade · Validate, Roll Back, FixDOWNGRADE ✓ checked vs PAN docs Runbook

Downgrading Across a Feature Release

Going back a whole floor means walking down every stair — and bringing your old rucksack (the config you exported) with you.

Dropping from 11.1 back to 10.2 is a different animal. Configuration introduced by the newer release has no meaning on the older one, so the automatic snapshot may not be usable.

  • You must downgrade through each feature release in reverse — the same staircase, going down.
  • Restore the pre-upgrade configuration you exported, not the current running config.
  • HA peers still cannot sit more than one feature release apart while you do it.
  • Content versions may need downgrading too if the newer content is incompatible with the older PAN-OS.
Load the config you exported before the upgrade:
admin@fw-01> scp import configuration from user@10.20.30.40:/backups/fw-01-pre.xml  copy a saved config file back ONTO the firewall
admin@fw-01> configure                                                        enter configuration mode — the prompt changes from > to #
admin@fw-01# load config from fw-01-pre.xml                                   load that file into the candidate config — still needs a commit
admin@fw-01# commit                                                           apply the candidate config — nothing above is live until this runs
admin@fw-01# exit                                                             leave configuration mode, back to the > prompt

This is why the off-box export in Backup is not optional. A cross-release downgrade without the original configuration file means rebuilding by hand under pressure. If you are seriously considering a feature-release downgrade during a change window, open a TAC case first.

  • Device → Setup → Operations → Import named configuration snapshot (your pre-upgrade export) → Load named configuration snapshot → Commit.
  • Installing an older feature release from Device → Software prompts you to pick the configuration to load — pick the pre-upgrade export.
Upgrade · Validate, Roll Back, FixDOWNLOAD ✓ checked vs PAN docs Runbook

Download and Install Failures

Error or symptomCause and fix
There is not enough free disk space to complete the desired operationExactly what it says. show system disk-space, then delete old images. Remember the 90% rule on pancfg.
Download job sits at ACT foreverNo route or DNS to the update servers from the management interface. Test with ping source <mgmt-ip> host updates.paloaltonetworks.com, and check the service route for Palo Alto Networks Services.
Download fails immediately, repeatedlyStale image list. request system software check to refresh, then retry. Also check licence and support entitlement — an expired support contract blocks software downloads outright.
Target version not listedMore than one feature release away. See The Upgrade Path.
Install rejected, base image missingDownload the base release, install nothing from it, retry the target.
Install job FIN/FAILRead the job details: show jobs id <jobid>. Usually disk, a corrupt download, or a failed pre-check. Delete and re-download the image before retrying.
Content install fails but download succeededpancfg near the 90% line. Clear old content, then reinstall.

A corrupt image is a real possibility on a flaky management link. delete software version <target> then download again — retrying the install against the same broken file will fail the same way every time.

Upgrade · Validate, Roll Back, FixPOST-REBOOT ✓ checked vs PAN docs Runbook

It Rebooted and Something Is Wrong

SymptomWhat to do
Never comes back at allConsole access. Boot messages tell you far more than a dead SSH session. This is why out-of-band access is first on the list.
SSH answers but no traffic passesshow chassis-ready. If it returns no, the dataplane is still coming up — wait. If it stays no, check show system software status and the system log.
Still on the old versionThe install job did not complete before the reboot. Re-run request system software install version <target> and wait for FIN/OK this time.
Interfaces down that were up beforeCompare against your baseline capture. Check the release notes for changes to default behaviour — interface or link-speed defaults do occasionally change between releases.
Processes restarting in a loopshow system software status, then the system log. Grab a tech-support file and open a TAC case rather than rebooting repeatedly.
Certificates rejected after upgradePAN-OS 11.1 and later enforce OpenSSL Security Level 2 — RSA 2048 / ECDSA 256 minimum, SHA256 digest or better. Weak certificates must be regenerated or re-imported.
Config partly missingDo not commit anything. Load your pre-upgrade export: load config from <file>, review, then commit.

When a firewall is misbehaving after an upgrade, the instinct is to reboot it again. Resist that. Each reboot destroys volatile state that TAC would use to diagnose the problem, and if a process is crash-looping, another reboot changes nothing. Capture a tech-support file first.

Upgrade · Validate, Roll Back, FixHA ✓ checked vs PAN docs Runbook

HA Problems During and After Upgrade

SymptomCause and fix
Peer version too old, peer suspends itselfPeers are two or more feature releases apart. Bring the lagging peer up one release. Unavoidable if you skipped a hop — you must finish the staircase.
Both peers active after rebootSplit brain from an HA1 control link failure. show high-availability all and check HA1, HA1-backup and heartbeat backup. Restore the control link, then suspend the peer that should not be active and make it functional again once HA1 is up.
Failover fired mid-upgradePreemption was never actually disabled, or the commit silently failed. show high-availability state | match Preempt. This is why the commit must be confirmed before you proceed.
Config out-of-sync after both peers upgradedFrom the peer you trust: request high-availability sync-to-remote running-config. Direction matters — see Force a Config Sync.
Upgraded peer will not go passiveIt is still suspended. request high-availability state functional. If it refuses, check show chassis-ready first — a peer with a dataplane that is not up cannot become functional.
Sessions drop on every failover afterwardsHA2 session sync is not running. show high-availability interface ha2 and confirm the counters increment. See Confirming Session Sync.
Pair never fails backPreemption left disabled after the window. Re-enable and commit.
HA links flapping post-upgradeLink or path monitoring was re-enabled while the dataplane was still settling. Confirm show chassis-ready on both, then re-check show high-availability path-monitoring.

Nearly every HA problem in this table traces back to one of three things: the peers are too far apart in version, something that should have been disabled was not, or something that should have been re-enabled was not. Check those three before reaching for anything clever.

Transcript — A 10.2.4-h32 to 10.2.13-h3 Pair

This transcript is a 10.2 run, kept because it is real. The commands, prompts and job behaviour are identical on 11.x and 12.1 — only the version strings change.

Edited from a real maintenance window on a PA-3410 active/passive pair. Hostnames and addresses are generic; the job IDs, errors and ordering are as they happened.

admin@fw-01(active)> request system software download version 10.2.13-h3  pull the image onto the firewall — non-disruptive, do it early
Download job enqueued with jobid 595
admin@fw-01(active)> request anti-virus upgrade download latest           fetch the newest antivirus signatures
Download job enqueued with jobid 596
admin@fw-01(active)> request wildfire upgrade download latest             fetch WildFire signatures — errors harmlessly without the licence
Server error : There is not wildfire license on the box   expected — no subscription
admin@fw-01(active)> request content upgrade download latest              fetch the newest Applications and Threats content
Download job enqueued with jobid 597

admin@fw-01(active)> show jobs id 595                                     poll that job until it reports FIN / OK
admin@fw-01(active)> show jobs id 596                                     poll that job until it reports FIN / OK
admin@fw-01(active)> show jobs id 597                                     poll that job until it reports FIN / OK
Same three downloads on the passive peer — separate job ID space per device:
admin@fw-02(passive)> request system software download version 10.2.13-h3  pull the image onto the firewall — non-disruptive, do it early
Download job enqueued with jobid 326
admin@fw-02(passive)> request anti-virus upgrade download latest           fetch the newest antivirus signatures
Download job enqueued with jobid 327
admin@fw-02(passive)> request content upgrade download latest              fetch the newest Applications and Threats content
Download job enqueued with jobid 328
Tech-support and content install on the active:
admin@fw-01(active)> request tech-support dump                          generate the diagnostic bundle TAC will ask for — do it BEFORE the change
Exec job enqueued with jobid 599
admin@fw-01(active)> request anti-virus upgrade install version latest  activate the antivirus signatures — no reboot needed
Content install job enqueued with jobid 600
admin@fw-01(active)> request content upgrade install version latest     activate the App and Threat content — no reboot needed
Content install job enqueued with jobid 601
Install on the suspended peer — note the confirmation prompt:
admin@fw-02(suspended)> request system software install version 10.2.13-h3  write the image to the spare partition — no effect until reboot
Executing this command will install a new version of software. It will not take
effect until system is restarted. Do you want to continue? (y or n)
Software install job enqueued with jobid 332. Run 'show jobs id 332' to monitor
its status. Please reboot the device after the installation is done.

Job IDs are per-device and unrelated between peers — 595 on one box and 326 on the other were the same operation. Track them per session, not globally, or you will poll the wrong job and conclude a download has stalled.

Commands That Are Wrong in Most Circulating Runbooks

These forms appear constantly in shared documents and internal wikis. They are legacy, mistyped, or environment-dependent. Verified against the current PAN-OS CLI reference.

Commonly writtenCorrect form / note
set ... high-availability group group-id 1 election-option preemptive noDrop the group ID: set deviceconfig high-availability group election-option preemptive no. Since PAN-OS 7.0 the HA group node is a singleton; group-id is a value you set under it, not an index. The old numbered form is PAN-OS 6.x and earlier.
show job id <jobid>show jobs id <jobid> — plural.
request wildfire upgrade download latestValid, but errors with There is not wildfire license on the box without the subscription. Skip it rather than treating the error as a fault.
request system software check (to list downloadables)check refreshes and shows what is loaded on the firewall; request system software info is the one that lists versions available for download with their Downloaded flag.
Install content, then assume HA syncs itContent is not synchronised by HA. Install on both peers explicitly.
Disable preemption on both peersOne peer is sufficient per Palo Alto's procedure. Both is harmless; the failure mode is doing neither and assuming.
Reboot immediately after the install command returnsThe command returns a job ID, not a result. Wait for show jobs id to report FIN/OK.
SSH answers, therefore the upgrade is doneManagement plane comes up first. Gate on show chassis-ready = yes.
configure → set max-num-images count 2 → commitset max-num-images count <2-64> is an operational-mode command. No configure, no commit. Check with show max-num-images.
request high-availability sessions-reestablish force (to fix split brain)Removed from this runbook — not a documented split-brain fix. Restore HA1 / HA1-backup, then suspend and re-functional the wrong active peer.
"You can never skip a feature release"Outdated. Skip Software Version (10.1 and later) allows direct jumps, e.g. 11.x → 12.1 on standalone and Panorama-managed firewalls. HA pairs: see Going to 12.1.
Upgrade · Validate, Roll Back, FixKNOW BEFORE YOU TYPE ✓ checked vs PAN docs Runbook

Commands That Bite

CommandWhat actually happens
request restart systemImmediate reboot, no confirmation, no grace period. On a standalone firewall this is the outage starting right now.
request high-availability state suspendRemoves the box from HA. Run it on the wrong peer and you have suspended the one carrying traffic while the other is mid-install.
request high-availability sync-to-remote running-configOverwrites the peer's running config with the local one. Direction is everything.
request system software installWrites to the alternate partition and marks it pending. Harmless until the reboot — but the next reboot for any reason will activate it.
commitOn an HA pair with config sync enabled, pushes to the peer as well. There is no "just on this box" commit.
set ... election-option preemptive yesIf the local box has higher priority, this can trigger an immediate failover on commit. Do it when you can tolerate one.
request system private-data-resetWipes configuration and logs to factory state. Present in the same command tree. Never during an upgrade.
load config from <file>Replaces the candidate config wholesale. The following commit replaces everything, including anything changed since the file was taken.
Upgrade · Validate, Roll Back, FixCOMMAND ORDER ✓ checked vs PAN docs Runbook

The Order That Works

HA pair, active/passive, single feature-release hop

01. show system info | match sw-version            both peers — baseline
02. show high-availability state                   both peers — must be in sync
03. save config to Pre_Upgrade_<date>.xml          both peers
04. scp export configuration ...                   both peers — off-box
04b. save device-state + scp export device-state both peers — full bundle
05. request tech-support dump                      both peers
06. request content upgrade download/install       both peers
07. request system software download version ...   both peers (or sync-to-peer yes)
08. show jobs id <jobid>                            confirm FIN/OK before continuing
09. set ... election-option preemptive no + commit one peer
10. request high-availability state suspend        peer A — verify traffic on peer B
11. request system software install version ...    peer A
12. request restart system                          peer A
13. show chassis-ready                              peer A — must be yes
14. request high-availability state functional     peer A — wait for sync
15. repeat 10-14 on peer B
16. set ... election-option preemptive yes + commit
17. post-upgrade validation

Standalone

01. baseline capture
02. save config + off-box export + tech-support
03. content download and install
04. request system software download version ...   plus base image if hotfix
05. show jobs id <jobid>
06. request system software install version ...
07. show jobs id <jobid>                            FIN/OK before rebooting
08. request restart system                          the outage
09. show chassis-ready + validation

The pattern behind both lists: everything non-disruptive happens first and can be done days ahead. The window itself should contain nothing but suspend, reboot and verify.

Panorama: Connection & Config AuditRECIPE ✓ checked vs PAN docs Recipe

Recipe: Adding a Firewall to Panorama

Use it when a firewall must be managed by Panorama. Since PAN-OS 10.1 the first connection is mutually authenticated with a device registration auth key generated on Panorama.

// on Panorama (operational): create a one-time device registration auth key
request authkey add devtype fw count 1 lifetime 60 name FW-ONBOARD serial 0123456789
request authkey list FW-ONBOARD
// on the firewall (configuration): point it at Panorama
configure
set deviceconfig system panorama local-panorama panorama-server 10.10.50.10
commit
exit
// on the firewall (operational): add the auth key
request authkey set <auth-key-from-Panorama>
show panorama-status
What each line does

Purpose: Creates a single-use auth key on Panorama, points the firewall at Panorama, installs the key, and checks the connection.

request authkey add devtype fw count 1 lifetime 60 name … serial …
A key for firewalls, usable once, valid for 60 minutes, and only for that serial (GUI: Panorama > Device Registration Auth Key).
request authkey list FW-ONBOARD
Shows the key value to copy.
set deviceconfig system panorama local-panorama panorama-server 10.10.50.10
The firewall's Panorama address (GUI: Device > Setup > Management > Panorama Settings). Add panorama-server-2 for an HA Panorama pair.
request authkey set <key>
Installs the key on the firewall. It must match one created on Panorama.
show panorama-status
Connected: yes when registration succeeded.

On Panorama: Panorama > Managed Devices > Summary > Add the firewall's serial number, commit, then place it in a device group and template stack.

Verify and troubleshoot

1 · Status

show panorama-status

Good: Panorama Server … Connected: yes. If not: Continue below.

2 · Reachability

ping host 10.10.50.10
show system info | match serial

Good: Panorama answers. The serial matches the one added on Panorama. If not: Management route/service route, or a firewall in between blocking TCP 3978.

3 · Auth key problems

request authkey list *

Good: The key is valid, not expired, has count left, and is for the right serial and device type. If not: Create a new key and run request authkey set again.

4 · Recover a broken secure connection (last resort)

request sc3 reset
debug software restart process management-server

Good: The device reconnects after a new auth key is set. If not: request sc3 reset is irreversible for the current connection. Follow Palo Alto's recovery procedure, including clear device-status on Panorama.

⚠ Syntax note. PAN-OS configuration-mode set commands. The structure follows Palo Alto documentation and published configurations. Use Tab/? while typing, run commit validate (or validate full) before commit, and check the GUI equivalent shown in each step.

Panorama: Connection & Config AuditROLLBACK ANCHOR ✓ checked vs PAN docs Lab · Edge HA pair

Save Before You Change Anything

Every bulk change starts with a named snapshot. It costs ten seconds and it is the difference between a rollback and an incident. Commands here are PAN-OS 11.x on Panorama.

CommandModeDescription / usage
save config to <filename>.xmlconfigSave the candidate to a named snapshot. Does not overwrite the default snapshot. Name it after the change — save config to pre-CHG44812.xml.
save config to running-config.xmlconfigSave the candidate into the default filename. Rarely what you want — named snapshots are better for a change window.
show config listconfigList saved named snapshots. Confirm your save landed before committing anything.
show config audit infoconfigThe automatic version history — every commit creates a numbered running-config version you can roll back to with no manual snapshot at all.
show config audit version <N>configContents of a specific historic version.
scp export configuration from <filename>.xml to <user>@<host>:<path>operationalExport a snapshot off-box. Strongly recommended before risky changes.
tftp export configuration from <filename>.xml to <tftp-host>operationalSame via TFTP where SCP is unavailable.
scp export config-bundle to <user>@<host>:<path>operationalPanorama only. A tarball containing Panorama's running config plus the running config of every managed firewall. The best single-file pre-change backup for an estate.
admin@panorama> configure
admin@panorama# save config to pre-CHG44812.xml
Config saved to pre-CHG44812.xml
admin@panorama# show config list
pre-CHG44812.xml
pre-CHG44190.xml
running-config.xml
admin@panorama# exit
admin@panorama> scp export configuration from pre-CHG44812.xml to jay@10.10.0.50:/backup/

A snapshot on Panorama is no help if Panorama is what breaks. Export it off-box, and set up a scheduled config export under Panorama > Setup > Operations so historic rollback files accumulate without anyone having to remember.

⚠ Verification note. save config to, show config saved and scp export configuration follow documented usage. show config audit info / version and scp export config-bundle (Panorama) weren't found in the official cheat sheets reviewed. Confirm with ? before using them in a change procedure. In the web interface, Config Audit (Device or Panorama > Config Audit) provides the same version comparison.

Validate and Preview Before Committing

CommandDescription / usageGUI path
validate fullValidate the entire candidate without committing. Catches the reference errors that make a commit fail. Always run before a large batch.Commit > Validate Changes
validate partial device-group <name>Validate only one device group's changes. Faster when the change is scoped.Commit > Commit Scope
show config diffExactly what the next commit will change — the CLI form of Preview Changes.Commit > Preview Changes
show jobs id <job-id>Result, warnings and errors from a commit or validate job. Read this after every commit.Tasks > select job
show jobs all | match CommitAll commit jobs — pending, running, completed, failed. Also answers "who committed what, when".Tasks
show system last-commit-infoJob ID, user and timing of the last commit. Works on Panorama and on a firewall.Tasks
request commit-lock add comment "<text>"Stop other admins committing while you stage. Release with request commit-lock remove.Padlock icon > Take Commit Lock
request config-lock add comment "<text>"Stop other admins editing the candidate. Different from a commit lock. Release with request config-lock remove.Padlock icon > Take Config Lock

Commit lock and config lock solve different problems. A config lock stops someone else adding changes to the candidate you are about to commit; a commit lock stops someone else pushing while you are mid-window. On shared Panorama, take both.

Panorama: Connection & Config AuditCOMMIT / PUSH ✓ checked vs PAN docs Lab · Edge HA pair

commit vs commit-all — The Distinction That Matters Most

These are two different operations and confusing them is the source of both "I committed and nothing changed" and, much worse, "I only meant to save it".

commitcommit-all
ModeConfigurationOperational
AffectsPanorama only — candidate becomes running on PanoramaThe managed firewalls
Changes production traffic?NoYes
PrerequisiteNoneA commit must have happened first (mandatory since PAN-OS 8.0)
CommandDescription / usage
commitPanorama-only commit. Use it to stage, save and peer-review without touching production.
commit description "<text>"Same, tagged with a description that lands in the audit log. Put the change number here.
commit admin <username>Partial commit — commit only one admin's changes. Essential when several people have pending edits and you do not want to publish somebody's work in progress.
commit partial device-and-network excludedPartial commit by scope. Note the CLI form takes exclusions, not inclusions. Scopes: device-and-network, shared-object, vsys, admin.
commit-all shared-policy device-group <DG>Push policy and objects to the firewalls in a device group. This is the one that changes traffic.
commit-all shared-policy device-group <DG> validate-only yesDry run. Validates the push without performing it. Catches missing objects, broken references and unsupported features before the window.
commit-all shared-policy device-group <DG> device <serial>Canary push to one named firewall inside the group. Verify, then push to the rest.
commit-all shared-policy device-group <DG> include-template yesPush device-group and its template config together. Use when network changes accompany the policy.
commit-all shared-policy device-group <DG> force-template-values yesOverride local values configured directly on the firewall. Destroys local overrides.
commit-all shared-policy device-group <DG> merge-with-candidate-cfg yesMerge with any pending local candidate on each firewall. The GUI default is yes.
commit-all template <template-name>Push template config only — interfaces, zones, system settings.
commit-all template-stack <stack-name>Push a template stack to its assigned firewalls.
commit-all log-collector-group <lcg-name>Push collector-group and log-forwarding config to log collectors.
admin@panorama# commit description "CHG44812 - add telemetry egress rule"
Commit job enqueued with jobid 88421
admin@panorama# exit
admin@panorama> commit-all shared-policy device-group DG-BRANCH validate-only yes   dry run first
Commit-all validation job enqueued with jobid 88422
admin@panorama> show jobs id 88422
88422  CommitAll  FIN  OK  Devices: 42 succeeded, 0 failed
admin@panorama> commit-all shared-policy device-group DG-BRANCH device 013201005678   canary
Commit-all job enqueued with jobid 88423
... verify on the canary ...
admin@panorama> commit-all shared-policy device-group DG-BRANCH                        full push

There is no single CLI equivalent of the GUI "Commit and Push" button. The GUI does both operations for you; the CLI does not. You must run commit first and commit-all second. Scripts that need the combined behaviour chain the two API calls.

commit is publishing the master copy. commit-all is posting it to every branch. Doing the first and forgetting the second is the most common form of "the change did not take" — and the reason a canary push exists is that discovering a bad change on one firewall is survivable, and discovering it on two hundred is not.

⚠ Verification note. The push options themselves (Merge with Device Candidate Config, Include Device and Network Templates, Force Template Values) are documented Palo Alto behaviour. The exact CLI keyword spellings after commit-all shared-policy device-group <DG> vary by Panorama release, so confirm them with ? before scripting.

Verifying a Push Landed

CommandRun onDescription / usage
show devicegroupsPanoramaAll device groups, their hierarchy and member serials. Confirm DG names before running commit-all.
show devicegroups name <device-group-name>PanoramaCommit history and connection status for the firewalls in one group.
show templates / show templates name <template>PanoramaTemplates and which firewalls or stacks reference them.
show template-stackPanoramaStacks and their member templates.

admin@panorama> show devices connected | match DG-BRANCH
serial          hostname        connected  sw-version  shared-policy-md5
013201005678    branch-fw-01    yes        11.1.4-h7   a41c8f...
013201005679    branch-fw-02    yes        11.1.4-h7   a41c8f...
013201005680    branch-fw-03    yes        11.1.4-h7   77b209...   <-- did not get the push

Comparing the shared-policy hash across a device group is the quickest way to spot a firewall that missed a push — far quicker than opening each one. A mismatch means either the device was disconnected at push time or its individual commit failed; show jobs all on that firewall will say which.

Panorama: Connection & Config AuditROLLBACK ✓ checked vs PAN docs Lab · Edge HA pair

The Rollback Playbook

CommandDescription / usage
revert configDiscard all uncommitted candidate changes. Config mode. Use this before commit when you realise the staged change is wrong.
load config version <N>Load a running-config audit version (number from show config audit info) into the candidate. The fastest rollback after a bad commit.
load config from <filename>.xmlLoad your named pre-change snapshot into the candidate.
load config last-savedLoad the most recent default snapshot. Equivalent to "Revert to last saved".
scp import configuration from <user>@<host>:<path>Import a previously exported XML snapshot. Then load config from <file> and commit.

Full rollback after a bad push

  1. show config audit info — identify the version number you want, usually N−1.
  2. load config version <N-1> — load it into the candidate.
  3. show config diff — confirm you are reverting what you think you are reverting.
  4. commit — activate the rollback on Panorama.
  5. commit-all shared-policy device-group <DG> — push it back out. Until you do this, the firewalls are still running the bad config.
  6. show jobs id <job-id> — confirm the push succeeded on every member.
admin@panorama# show config audit info
version  date                  admin   description
412      2026-04-27 15:04:11   jay     CHG44812 - add telemetry egress rule
411      2026-04-26 09:22:03   dsingh  CHG44790 - branch URL profile
admin@panorama# load config version 411
Config loaded from version 411
admin@panorama# show config diff
admin@panorama# commit description "ROLLBACK CHG44812"

Step 5 is the one people forget. Loading the old version and committing it fixes Panorama and nothing else. The firewalls keep running the pushed config until commit-all replaces it. Rehearse the exact sequence before the change window, not during it.

Panorama: Connection & Config AuditBEST PRACTICE ✓ checked vs PAN docs Lab · Edge HA pair

Bulk Change Workflow

  1. save config to <name>.xml — the rollback anchor.
  2. Make the changes with set commands.
  3. show config diff — read what you are about to do.
  4. validate full — catch reference errors now, not during the push.
  5. commit description "CHG#####" — Panorama only. Nothing has reached production yet.
  6. scp export configuration from <name>.xml to ... — off-box copy.
  7. commit-all ... validate-only yes — dry run the push.
  8. commit-all ... device <canary-serial> — one firewall.
  9. Verify on the canary.
  10. commit-all ... — the full device group.
  11. show jobs id <job-id> — confirm every member succeeded.

Steps 1–6 are non-disruptive and can be done days ahead. Only steps 7–11 need the change window. Splitting the work that way keeps the risk window down to minutes and decouples your preparation from whenever the customer will actually let you push — which is usually the constraint that matters.

A scheduled config export under Panorama > Setup > Operations > Schedule Config Export gives you historic rollback files for free and removes the "did anyone take a backup" question from every change entirely.

Panorama: Connection & Config AuditTECHNIQUE ✓ checked vs PAN docs Lab · Edge HA pair

Fleet-Wide Keyword Hunt From the Panorama CLI

Search every template and template stack for a configuration keyword in one pass, from the Panorama CLI. No jump server, no scripts, no API. The primary use is CVE exposure checking across a large managed estate, but it works for any hardening or audit question.

The three moves

  1. Set the output format. set cli config-output-format set — operational mode, before configure. This is what makes grep useful: every leaf prints as a full set template <name> ... <value> line, so a match shows which template owns the hit and what the value is.
  2. Confirm the keyword. find command keyword <keyword> in configure mode reveals the valid paths — template vs template-stack, which vsys level — so you know what to search for before you search.
  3. Search both containers. show template | match <keyword> and then show template-stack | match <keyword>.
CommandModeDescription / usage
set cli config-output-format setoperationalPrint config as runnable set commands. Session-scoped.
set cli config-output-format defaultoperationalRevert when finished.
set cli pager offoperationalStop paging on large dumps. Per-command alternative: append | no-more.
find command keyword <keyword>configureFind every command path containing the keyword.
show template | match <keyword>configureSearch every template in one command — template config lives inside Panorama's own config tree.
show template-stack | match <keyword>configureThe companion search for stacks.
show template <name> | match <keyword>configureScope to one template for a spot check.
show config running | match <keyword>operationalGrep the whole running config — broader and noisier, but catches device-groups and shared objects too.

Stack-level overrides do not appear in show template. You must run show template-stack as well. Skipping the second command is the standard gap that lets a stack-pushed setting slip past an audit and produce a confident, wrong "we are not exposed".

Panorama: Connection & Config AuditINTERPRETATION ✓ checked vs PAN docs Lab · Edge HA pair

Reading the Output — Empty Container vs Real Entry

A match is not the same as an exposure. PAN-OS emits a node line for a feature container even when nothing was ever configured inside it — someone opened the tab once and the empty node persisted.

admin@panorama# show template | match ts-agent
set template T-BRANCH-EU config vsys vsys1 ts-agent                               <-- BARE NODE. Empty container.
set template T-DC-CORE config vsys vsys1 ts-agent TSA-01 host 10.10.0.60          <-- REAL ENTRY
set template T-DC-CORE config vsys vsys1 ts-agent TSA-01 port 5009
set template T-DC-CORE config vsys vsys1 ts-agent TSA-01 disabled no              <-- and it is live
Output shapeVerdictWhat the GUI shows
Nothing returnedNot configured. Clean.Feature tab absent or empty.
Bare node line only — keyword with nothing after itEmpty container. Not configured, not exposed.Tab present, no rows.
Node plus value lines (host, port, ip-list)Real entry. Configured.Rows present.
Real entry with disabled yesConfigured but inactive. Lower priority than a live one, but still remediate.ENABLED column = no.

The rule of thumb: if grep returns nothing, or only bare nodes, you are clean. Value lines mean somebody actually configured the thing.

Panorama: Connection & Config AuditWORKED EXAMPLE ✓ checked vs PAN docs Lab · Edge HA pair

Worked Example — Terminal Server Agent Exposure Check

An advisory lands naming the User-ID Terminal Server Agent component, with an exposure gate: a firewall is only affected if a TS Agent is actually configured. Panorama itself is not impacted. The keyword to hunt is ts-agent — not user-id-agent, which is a different component entirely.

  1. Version filter. show devices all lists every managed firewall with serial and PAN-OS version. Flag anything below the fixed build for its train.
  2. Fleet-wide config hunt. After set cli config-output-format set, run both show template | match ts-agent and show template-stack | match ts-agent. Bare nodes or no results across both means no template-pushed TSA anywhere.
  3. Per-device fallback. show user ts-agent state all on each firewall catches local on-box TSA config that Panorama never pushed and therefore cannot see. Empty output means no TSA on that box. Reach each firewall through the Panorama context switcher rather than a jump host. Related: show user ts-agent statistics.
admin@panorama> set cli config-output-format set
admin@panorama> configure
admin@panorama# show template | match ts-agent
set template T-BRANCH-EU config vsys vsys1 ts-agent
admin@panorama# show template-stack | match ts-agent
(no output)
admin@panorama# exit
admin@panorama> -- context switch to a firewall --
admin@dc-fw-01> show user ts-agent state all
No Terminal Server Agents configured

Verdict from the above: one bare node, no stack entries, nothing on-box. Not exposed via configuration. The version-patching work still stands on its own schedule — the config hunt tells you how urgent it is, not whether you can skip it.

Where a configured box cannot be patched immediately, the interim mitigation is to restrict TSA connectivity to trusted internal addresses using the trusted-source-address list. That reduces exposure and does not remove the underlying bug — still schedule the vendor patch.

Fixed-version lists and advisory details change as vendors publish revisions. Always confirm the current fixed builds against the live Palo Alto security advisory for the CVE you are chasing rather than a number copied into a runbook.

Panorama: Connection & Config AuditREUSABLE ✓ checked vs PAN docs Lab · Edge HA pair

The Reusable Pattern

The same three moves work for any configuration keyword. Swap the keyword for whatever the advisory or the hardening standard names, and confirm the exact leaf with find command keyword first.

set cli config-output-format set
configure
find command keyword <X>              confirm the exact leaf keyword
show template | match <X>
show template-stack | match <X>
exit
set cli config-output-format default   put it back
KeywordAudits
globalprotect / global-protectGP portal and gateway configuration — a recurring CVE target.
ssl-decryptWhere decryption is enabled across the estate.
telnet / httpManagement-profile hardening. Neither should be enabled anywhere.
snmpSNMP community strings and versions in use.
clientless-vpnClientless VPN, another recurring advisory subject.
wildfireWildFire forwarding configuration and cloud selection.
permitted-ipManagement-interface access lists — find the templates with none.

The value of this technique is not that it is clever — it is that it turns "we think we are fine" into a piece of evidence with template names on it, in about ninety seconds, without a single script or credential outside the Panorama session you already had.

Field ReferenceCORRECTIONS ✓ checked vs PAN docs Lab · Edge HA pair

Syntax That Is Wrong in Circulating Cheat Sheets

These forms appear widely in shared PAN-OS command lists. They are wrong or misleading, and they are listed rather than silently fixed because you will meet them in other people's documents.

Frequently seenCorrect formWhy it matters
show counter global filter aspect drop delta yesshow counter global filter severity drop delta yesdrop is a severity value, not an aspect value. Aspect takes processing stages — parse, session, forward, pktproc. The wrong form returns nothing and reads as a healthy firewall.
show high-availability flap statisticsshow high-availability flap-statisticsHyphenated. As two words the parser rejects it.
set system setting arp-cache-timeout <60-65535>set system setting arp-cache-timeout <60-65536>Minor, but the documented upper bound is 65536.
set commands assumed to be config-modeset system setting ..., set cli ... are operational modeRejected in # mode. They are runtime settings, not staged config, and are never committed.
tcpdump used for transit trafficdebug dataplane packet-diagtcpdump captures the management interface only. It will never show traffic passing through the firewall.
Turning the packet-diag filter off before the logLog off first, then filter offWith no filter, every packet matches. Turning the filter off while logging is on briefly logs the entire box.
Legacy show routing ... on an Advanced Routing boxshow advanced-routing ...Returns an empty table rather than an error, which reads as "no routes" instead of "wrong command".
Expecting a CLI "Commit and Push"commit then commit-allThe combined GUI button has no single CLI equivalent. Two commands, in that order.
Auditing with show template aloneAlso show template-stackStack-level overrides are invisible to show template.
set cli config-output-mode setset cli config-output-format setBoth are accepted; config-output-mode appears in the Panorama cheat sheet, while the knowledge base and every other reference use config-output-format. Use the latter to avoid confusion.
Field ReferenceDANGER ✓ checked vs PAN docs Lab · Edge HA pair

Commands That Bite

None of these prompt for confirmation. All of them are one keystroke away from something you meant to type.

CommandWhat actually happensDo this instead
clear session allEvery session on the box is torn down. Every user reconnects.clear session all filter source <ip>, or clear session id <id>
clear vpn ike-saEvery Phase 1 SA drops. On a hub, that is every branch.clear vpn ike-sa gateway <name>
clear vpn ipsec-saEvery Phase 2 SA drops.clear vpn ipsec-sa tunnel <name>
clear arp allWhole ARP table flushed. Every flow pauses to re-resolve.clear arp <interface> <ip>
clear user-cache allAll user mappings dropped. User-based policy fails until re-learned.Target the specific IP, or wait for the refresh.
debug software restart process allEvery management process restarts.Restart the one process, after taking a tech-support file.
debug software restart dataplaneDataplane restarts. All sessions drop.Suspend HA first if there is a peer.
request system private-data-resetConfiguration and logs wiped to factory.Almost never. Confirm with TAC.
commit-all ... force-template-values yesLocal overrides on every target firewall are destroyed.Push to a canary first and look at what changed.
debug dataplane packet-diag set log on with a wide filterDataplane CPU spike on a production box.Narrow the filter to one 5-tuple, and keep it to seconds.
Pre-Parse MatchCaptures everything regardless of filter. Extremely heavy.Only when TAC asks for it.

The pattern across the whole table: the dangerous form is the one with no argument. clear with a target is a scalpel; clear without one is a fire axe. If your finger is heading for Enter on a bare clear, stop and add a filter.

Close-Out Checklist

Run through this before you close the ticket. Every item is something that survives your SSH session and affects the next person.

CheckCommand

Every daemon debug level back to defaultdebug <process> off · debug routing global on info · debug ike global on info

Findings written down while they are fresh—

The one that causes the most downstream trouble is a leftover packet-diag filter. It is invisible in the GUI dashboard, it survives your session, and it makes the next person's captures return either nothing or somebody else's traffic. Always confirm with debug dataplane packet-diag show setting rather than trusting that clear all did its job.

Field ReferenceGLOSSARY ✓ checked vs PAN docs NAT guides

Acronyms and Jargon

From the Destination NAT material

TermStands forWhat it means here
DNATDestination NATRewriting the destination so outside clients reach an internal server.
Pre-NAT / post-NAT—Before / after translation. PAN-OS rules use pre-NAT addresses; security uses the post-NAT zone.
Post-NAT zone—The zone of the translated destination, found by a second route lookup.
Static IP (destination)—1:1 destination translation; single IP, range or netmask of equal size.
Translated port—The internal port for port translation; blank keeps the original port.
Dynamic IP (with session distribution)—Destination translation to an FQDN or dynamic group, spreading sessions across its addresses.
Distribution method—Round Robin, Source IP Hash, IP Modulo, IP Hash, Least Sessions.
Bi-directional—Static source NAT option that creates an implied inbound translation.
Double NATalso twice NATTranslating both source and destination, needed when subnets truly overlap.
ND / NS / NB—Session flags: destination NAT, source NAT, both.
Proxy ARP—The firewall answering ARP for a NAT address in the interface's subnet.
Proxy-ID—Local/remote subnet pair of an IPsec phase 2 SA.
FQDNFully Qualified Domain NameA DNS name used as an address object; resolved by the firewall.
ADCApplication Delivery ControllerA dedicated load balancer (e.g. F5 BIG-IP) with health checks and SSL offload.
U-turn NATalso hairpin NATInternal clients reaching a published server via its public address. Next guide.

From the Source NAT material

TermStands forWhat it means here
NAT / SNAT / DNAT(Source / Destination) Network Address TranslationRewriting addresses; SNAT changes the source, DNAT the destination.
DIPPDynamic IP and PortMany-to-few translation with port translation; the default PAN-OS source NAT.
DIPDynamic IP1:1 dynamic address translation without port change; drops when exhausted unless DIPP fallback is set.
Static IP—Fixed 1:1 mapping of address or equal-sized range; source port kept.
Bi-directional—Static IP option that also creates the reverse (inbound) translation.
Oversubscription—Reusing one translated address/port pair for several concurrent sessions to different destinations.
Interface Address—DIPP using the egress interface's own IP.
Translated Address—DIPP/DIP/Static using a specified address or pool.
Pre-NAT / post-NAT—The packet before or after translation. Security rules use pre-NAT addresses and post-NAT zones.
Zone—A group of interfaces; every rule matches from-zone and to-zone.
c2s / s2cclient-to-server / server-to-clientThe two flows of a session, shown by show session id.
NS / ND / NB—Session flags: source NAT, destination NAT, both.
Proxy ARP—The firewall answering ARP for a translated address in the interface subnet.
Proxy-ID—Local/remote subnet pair for an IPsec phase 2 SA; must use translated ranges when NAT is applied.
Candidate / running config—Your edits vs what the firewall is actually using. commit moves one to the other.
packet-diag—PAN-OS dataplane capture and counter tool, per stage (receive, firewall, transmit, drop).
App-ID—Application identification; a security-rule match field, never a NAT field.
VR / LRVirtual Router / Logical RouterRouting instance (legacy engine / advanced routing engine).

From the U-turn NAT material

TermStands forWhat it means here
U-turn NATalso hairpin NAT, NAT loopbackInternal clients reaching an internal server via its public address.
DIPPDynamic IP and PortSource NAT with port translation; used on the U-turn rule to force a symmetric return.
NB / NS / ND—Session flags: both, source, destination NAT.
Pre-NAT / post-NAT zone—NAT rules use the zone of the original destination; security uses the zone of the translated one.
Intrazone-default—Built-in rule allowing traffic within the same zone unless overridden.
Asymmetric routing—Request and reply taking different paths; the reason U-turn needs source NAT.
DNS proxy—PAN-OS feature answering client DNS queries, with optional static entries.
Split DNSalso split-horizonDifferent DNS answers inside and outside for the same name.
First match—NAT rules are evaluated top-down; the first matching rule applies.
FQDNFully Qualified Domain NameThe full hostname, e.g. app.example.com.
packet-diag—PAN-OS dataplane capture and counter tool.
Field ReferenceREFRESHER ✓ checked vs PAN docs

Twenty Questions to Check Your Understanding

QuestionAnswer
Which IPs and zone does a security rule match with DNAT?Pre-NAT IPs, post-NAT destination zone.
Which destination zone does a DNAT NAT rule use?The zone from routing the pre-NAT destination (often UNTRUST).
When is the address actually rewritten?At egress, after all decisions.
What decides the destination zone?The route lookup (or PBF) → egress interface → its zone.
Default AD for OSPF internal on a legacy VR?30 (external 110).
Is ECMP on by default on a VR?No. It must be enabled.
What does the A flag mean in show routing route?Active: the route forwards traffic.
How do you see the egress for one IP?test routing fib-lookup virtual-router <vr> ip <ip>
Why does ping from the CLI "work" but prove nothing?Without source it uses the management interface.
Which counter says "denied by a rule"?flow_policy_deny.
Which counter signals asymmetric routing?flow_tcp_non_syn_drop.
What does session state DISCARD mean?The firewall decided to drop that flow.
Why is denied traffic often missing from the traffic log?interzone-default doesn't log unless overridden.
What allows spoke-to-spoke at the hub in this lab?intrazone-default allow (VPN → VPN).
Which four capture stages exist?receive, firewall, transmit, drop.
Why clear the session before capturing?Existing sessions may be offloaded or use the fast path.
What must proxy-IDs on two peers look like?Mirrors: local ↔ remote.
Same-subnet U-turn needs what extra?Source NAT as well as destination NAT.
Where must next-vr routes exist?In both VRs, for both directions.
Where do you troubleshoot in an HA pair?On the active firewall.

Sources and Scope

SourceCovers
PAN-OS CLI Quick Start — CLI Cheat Sheets (Networking, HA, Panorama, Device Management, Vsys, User-ID)Command syntax, Advanced Routing tree, BFD, ARP cache timeout, netstat, cluster commands.
Palo Alto Networks Knowledge BaseGlobal counter semantics, config output formats, packet-diag workflow, session interpretation.
PAN-OS 11 Panorama documentationCommit operations, save and export, commit-all options, rollback.
Palo Alto Networks security advisoriesCVE detail and fixed builds. Always check the live advisory rather than a copied version list.

Commands here were checked against current Palo Alto documentation at the time of writing and apply to PAN-OS 10.1 through 11.2 unless a topic states otherwise. CLI syntax does move between feature releases — when a command is rejected, ? at any point in the tree shows exactly what the box in front of you accepts, and find command keyword <text> finds where it moved to.

Two habits outlast any command list. Ask the firewall rather than guessing — test, ? and find command keyword exist for exactly that. And clean up after yourself, every time, because the next person to troubleshoot this box may well be you.

Coverage, Verification and Upkeep

  • Behaviour and commands are checked against Palo Alto Networks TechDocs and Knowledge Base articles for PAN-OS 10.x–11.x. Legacy virtual-router commands come first, with Advanced Routing Engine equivalents noted.
  • Sample outputs are realistic and use the lab addressing. Where layouts vary between releases, blocks say "illustrative" or "trimmed". Read field names, not column positions.
  • Lab configs use the documented set structure. Run commit validate on a lab box before using them as a template.

How to keep it reliable

  1. Re-check on each PAN-OS release you deploy: read "Changes to default behaviour" and add anything affecting routing, NAT, policy or sessions to the upgrade playbook.
  2. Turn every escalation into a playbook entry: symptom, the counter or test that found it, the fix, the evidence.
  3. Keep the lab baseline as the single source of truth. New scenarios change one line.

Customer recommendations derived from this guide should still go through your normal review process before implementation. The guide provides the evidence and the options. The change decision stays with the process.
